Theme

School & learning

head teacher noun

also headteacher, headmaster, headmistress, principal, head of school, assistant principal, vice principal, deputy head, principal’s office

modern

Traupman 31: (lūdī or scholae) rēctor, fem. rēctrīx
Traupman 326

scholae rēctor, rēctōris m.

head of a school

Rēctor is classical for a guide or director (Cic., Lewis & Short); Traupman gives it for the principal, with lūdī or scholae, and rēctrīx for a woman. The head’s office is rēctōris conclāve.

Other words

  • scholarcha, scholarchae m./f.

    also used · modern · Andresian p. 13; M-O s.v. principal, headmaster · Declension on Wiktionary

    A Greek-looking coinage, not in Lewis & Short.

  • gymnasiarchus, gymnasiarchī m. — master of a gymnasium

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.92 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. principal, headmaster · Declension on Wiktionary

    Cicero’s word for the head of a Greek gymnasium; Morgan–Owens takes it for a headmaster. It suits a grammar school better than a primary school.

  • rēctor (rēctrīx) vicārius (vicāria) — assistant or deputy head

    also used · modern · Traupman 28, 31, 402 · Wiktionary

    Vicārius is classically a substitute or deputy.

  • rēctōris (rēctrīcis) officīna — the head’s office

    avoid · modern · Traupman 31 · Wiktionary

    Officīna is classically a workshop or factory (Lewis & Short), not an office; say conclāve rēctōris.

See also teacher, school, pupil.
